_purpose: Machine-readable state schema for LNES-60 Physical Truth. R&D/DESIGNED, not implemented in production. Companion to LNES60_PHYSICAL_TRUTH_ARCHITECTURE.md.
_governing_principle: Never encode SENSOR_ALWAYS_WINS. Verified physical evidence may invalidate a document-derived operational conclusion only when the witness's identity, calibration, freshness, integrity, scope, and applicability are established.

documentary_state.temporal_note: Historical records within this plane are immutable once committed; current-state conclusions derived FROM them are separately time-indexed and may become stale without altering the historical record itself.

physical_witness_state.requires: witness_trust_state (a physical_witness_state reading without an associated, currently-valid witness_trust_state record is not admissible evidence -- see LNES60_WITNESS_TRUST_MODEL.md)

witness_trust_state.role: Governs whether a physical_witness_state reading is admissible and how much weight it carries. Distinct from cryptographic integrity (a signature proves origin/non-tampering, not trustworthiness of the underlying measurement).

VERIFIED_MATCH.meaning: Documentary, command, and physical witness planes agree, and the witness trust state is fully established (identity, calibration, freshness, scope all valid).
VERIFIED_MATCH.release_implication: Eligible input to RELEASE_ELIGIBLE, subject to LNES-22's own separate policy evaluation.

DOCUMENT_PHYSICAL_CONFLICT.meaning: A trusted physical witness reading contradicts a documentary-derived current-state conclusion. The documentary record itself is NOT altered (see documentary_state.temporal_note) -- only the current-state conclusion is marked in conflict.

CONFIGURATION_MISMATCH.meaning: Command/digital state (e.g. expected_hardware_ids, firmware) does not match physical witness hardware_identity or another verified plane.

SENSOR_CONFLICT.meaning: Two or more currently-valid, currently-trusted witnesses for the same measurement scope disagree with each other.
SENSOR_CONFLICT.release_implication: HOLD -- the conflict is preserved, not resolved by picking one sensor (see failure taxonomy item 13).

SENSOR_DEGRADED.meaning: A witness's trust state indicates reduced but non-zero confidence (e.g. sensor_health below nominal, elevated measurement_uncertainty) -- not fully disqualifying, but not full-weight evidence either.
SENSOR_DEGRADED.release_implication: Context-dependent per LNES-22 policy; not itself sufficient for RELEASE_ELIGIBLE without corroboration.

STALE_WITNESS.meaning: A witness reading's freshness has lapsed relative to a subsequent event that could have changed physical reality (e.g. a hard landing occurring after the reading -- see failure taxonomy item 5), OR relative to a fixed validity window regardless of intervening events.
STALE_WITNESS.release_implication: Not admissible as current evidence; does not by itself invalidate the underlying historical reading.

WITNESS_SCOPE_ERROR.meaning: A witness reading's measurement_scope or aircraft_component_binding does not cover the entity/predicate being evaluated (e.g. a reading bound to the wrong component, or a reading whose scope is narrower than the claim being checked -- see failure taxonomy item 8).
WITNESS_SCOPE_ERROR.release_implication: Not admissible for the claim in question; may remain valid evidence for its actual scope.

UNVERIFIED.meaning: A claim exists in one or more planes but the witness trust state required to evaluate it has not been established (e.g. calibration record missing).
UNVERIFIED.release_implication: HOLD or INCOMPLETE depending on whether verification is in-progress or unavailable.

INCOMPLETE.meaning: Required evidence across the planes has not been fully gathered -- structurally distinct from UNVERIFIED (evidence present but not trust-verified) and from a NO_MATCH-style negative finding (evidence gathering complete, nothing found).
INCOMPLETE.release_implication: Never resolves to RELEASE_ELIGIBLE by default.

RELEASE_ELIGIBLE.meaning: Terminal engineering-authorization output: no unresolved conflict, no stale/out-of-scope/unverified witness blocking the claim, planes reconciled per the governing principle.
RELEASE_ELIGIBLE.explicit_non_claim: This is an ENGINEERING authorization output, not autonomous regulatory return-to-service and not a substitute for any legally required inspection or human signoff. LNES-22 performs its own separate policy evaluation before any action authority is granted.

HOLD.meaning: Terminal engineering-authorization output: a conflict or unresolved condition exists that must not be silently resolved.
HOLD.explicit_non_claim: A HOLD from LNES-60 does not itself take any physical action -- it is a state, consumed by LNES-22, which determines actual system behavior.

engineering_envelope_discipline.rule: No universal safety thresholds are hardcoded in this schema or its companion documents (e.g. no fixed tether-elongation percentage, pawl-tolerance millimeter value, or print-deviation temperature is asserted as a real engineering limit).
engineering_envelope_discipline.representation: All numeric thresholds used anywhere in the LNES-60 test harness are represented as ENGINEERING_ENVELOPE parameters, explicitly labeled synthetic, supplied per test case -- never as defaults implying real qualified engineering data.

engineering_envelope.label: MUST be one of: 'SYNTHETIC_TEST_VALUE' | 'QUALIFIED_ENGINEERING_DATA' (the latter never used by this schema's own test harness, reserved for a future real-data integration explicitly out of scope here)
engineering_envelope.source: string, free text, e.g. 'LNES60_KTX_TEST_MATRIX.md test class 1'

witness_envelope_type_discipline.rule: Every witness object carries an explicit type tag distinguishing simulated from hardware-sourced data.
witness_envelope_type_discipline.hard_rule: SIMULATED_WITNESS data must never be presented, logged, or reported as HARDWARE_WITNESS (aircraft telemetry) data, anywhere in the system or its outputs.
